From the issuing corporation's point of.It avoids fixed payments, and dividends: Dividends paid on stock are not deductible to the corporation; only bond interest is.
From the issuing corporation's point of.It requires fixed payments, but dividend: This reverses both points: stock needs no fixed payments, and its dividends are not deductible.
From the issuing corporation's point of.It requires fixed payments, and interest: That describes debt financing, not equity.

Rafael, age 61, plans to retire in two y.A national automaker: Automakers are cyclical: profits rise in expansions and fall in downturns.
Rafael, age 61, plans to retire in two y.A casual-dining restaurant chain: Restaurants are cyclical consumer discretionary businesses that suffer in recessions.
Rafael, age 61, plans to retire in two y.An emerging robotics developer: An emerging growth/technology company carries high risk and is not defensive.

Brightway Corp. pays for a large expansi.Market risk: Market risk comes from broad market moves, not from how this firm finances itself.
Brightway Corp. pays for a large expansi.Business risk: Business risk relates to the firm's operations and management, not its choice of debt over equity.
Brightway Corp. pays for a large expansi.Interest rate risk: Rate changes affect all stocks; the specific risk added by borrowing is financial (leverage) risk.

Which feature is typical of a warrant bu.An exercise price below the stock's mark: A below-market exercise price describes rights, not warrants.
Which feature is typical of a warrant bu.A life of only a few weeks before it exp: A very short life describes rights; warrants usually run for years.
Which feature is typical of a warrant bu.An offer to existing holders to keep the: Rights are offered to current shareholders to preserve their percentage ownership.

Which statement correctly contrasts a wa.The warrant usually expires within nine: Calls usually expire within nine months; warrants typically last several years.
Which statement correctly contrasts a wa.The warrant's terms are standardized by: Standardized OCC terms describe listed calls; warrants are customized.
Which statement correctly contrasts a wa.The warrant is written by an individual: Calls are written by individuals; warrants are issued by the corporation.

Which of the following defines the ex-di.The day the company's books are checked: That describes the record date, when settled owners appear on the books.

Mateo wants to receive the next quarterl.Buying on Wednesday at the market open: Any purchase on the ex-dividend date comes without the dividend, even at the open.
Mateo wants to receive the next quarterl.Buying on Wednesday just before the clos: Shares bought on the ex-dividend date do not carry the dividend.
Mateo wants to receive the next quarterl.Buying on Thursday, the day after the ex: Purchases after the ex-dividend date are not entitled to the declared dividend.

Tallis Inc. is worth $24 million and has.$14.40: A stock dividend lowers the price per share; it does not raise it by 20%.

Priya owns 200 shares of Norland Co. tha.300 shares at $90; basis $30 per share: The price must fall when shares increase; total value stays at $18,000.

For a common-stock dividend to receive q.More than 12 months before the dividend: The 12-month rule is for long-term capital gains on sales, not the dividend holding test.

For a common-stock dividend to receive q.More than 60 days in the 121-day window: The window starts 60 days before the ex-dividend date, not on the record date.

Hal has $1,200 of dividends reinvested t.No tax is due until he sells the shares: Reinvested dividends are taxed in the year paid, just like cash dividends.
Hal has $1,200 of dividends reinvested t.Tax is due on the $1,200 now, but his ba: Reinvested dividends are added to basis, which prevents double taxation when he sells.
Hal has $1,200 of dividends reinvested t.No tax is due now, and his basis rises b: Reinvestment doesn't defer tax; the dividend is taxable in the year paid.

Corin Corp. pays a 10% stock dividend, a.Taxed now as a qualified dividend at the: A stock dividend with no cash option is generally not taxable when received.
Corin Corp. pays a 10% stock dividend, a.Taxed now as ordinary income at the new: No income is recognized; the holder owns the same share of the company.
Corin Corp. pays a 10% stock dividend, a.No tax now; the new shares have a zero b: Basis is not zero; total basis is reallocated across all shares, lowering basis per share.

The Aldergrove Fund holds securities wor.$18.98: This leaves out the $2.4 million of cash; total assets include everything the fund owns.
The Aldergrove Fund holds securities wor.$19.53: This uses only the securities and ignores both cash and liabilities.
The Aldergrove Fund holds securities wor.$20.55: This counts all assets but forgets to subtract the $1.3 million of liabilities.

Claire enters an order at 11:15 a.m. ET.The NAV computed at the prior day's clos: Mutual funds use forward pricing, not the last computed NAV.
Claire enters an order at 11:15 a.m. ET.The fund's NAV at the moment her order i: Open-end funds don't price continuously; they price at the next calculation.
Claire enters an order at 11:15 a.m. ET.A market price set by supply and demand: That describes closed-end funds and ETFs, not open-end funds.

Gwen, age 40, will put a large sum into.Class B shares with a contingent deferre: B shares avoid an up-front load but generally cost more in total than A shares.
Gwen, age 40, will put a large sum into.Class C shares with a level asset-based: C shares charge an ongoing 12b-1 sales fee every year, which adds up over long horizons.
Gwen, age 40, will put a large sum into.Whichever class has the smallest up-fron: Total cost over the holding period matters, not just the initial charge.

Teresa, an Oregon resident in a high tax.A national municipal bond fund: Most of a national fund's interest is subject to state tax; only the Oregon-issuer portion would be exempt.
Teresa, an Oregon resident in a high tax.A GNMA mortgage-backed securities fund: GNMA fund income is federally taxable.
Teresa, an Oregon resident in a high tax.An investment-grade corporate bond fund: Corporate bond interest is federally taxable.

Nolan, an Ohio resident, received $2,400.$0: The fund reports the in-state share precisely so residents can exempt it from state tax.
Nolan, an Ohio resident, received $2,400.$2,040: That is the out-of-state portion (85%), which is subject to Ohio tax.
Nolan, an Ohio resident, received $2,400.$2,400: Only the share from Ohio issuers is state-exempt; a national fund is not fully exempt.

What does a target-date (lifecycle) fund.A fixed risk level the investor picks: c: Choosing a fixed risk level describes a lifestyle fund.
What does a target-date (lifecycle) fund.Moving up to 100% into stocks, bonds or: That describes a flexible portfolio fund.
What does a target-date (lifecycle) fund.Holding about 60% stocks and 40% bonds a: A steady 60/40 mix describes a typical balanced fund.

Which feature distinguishes a closed-end.It continuously issues new shares to mee: Continuous issuance describes open-end funds; closed-end capital is fixed after the IPO.
Which feature distinguishes a closed-end.Investors redeem their shares directly w: Closed-end shares are sold to other investors in the market, not redeemed with the fund.
Which feature distinguishes a closed-end.Its share count rises and falls daily wi: A changing share count describes open-end funds.

Which statement about unit investment tr.A board of directors oversees the trust': UITs have no board, no corporate officers and no investment advisor.
Which statement about unit investment tr.The portfolio is actively traded in resp: UITs are passive: the portfolio is selected once and then held.
Which statement about unit investment tr.The trust continues indefinitely, like a: UITs have a limited, specified life and liquidate at the end of their term.

Marcus has $600,000 to invest. He wants.A large-cap index mutual fund: A fund holder owns a share of a pool, can't exclude holdings and has no lot-level basis.
Marcus has $600,000 to invest. He wants.A unit investment trust: A UIT's portfolio is fixed at the start; it can't be customized or actively managed for taxes.
Marcus has $600,000 to invest. He wants.A closed-end fund: A closed-end fund is still a pooled portfolio with no individual cost basis or exclusions.

Which feature mainly makes ETFs more tax.A legal exemption from distributing capi: ETFs have no such exemption; their structure simply tends to produce fewer gains.
Which feature mainly makes ETFs more tax.They pay only qualified dividends: Nothing restricts ETFs to qualified dividends; that depends on what they hold.
Which feature mainly makes ETFs more tax.Forward pricing once at each day's close: ETFs trade all day at market prices; forward pricing applies to mutual funds.

Sofia wants low-cost, broad index exposu.An S&amp;P 500 index mutual fund: A mutual fund is priced once a day and can't be bought on margin or sold short like an exchange-traded share.
Sofia wants low-cost, broad index exposu.A stock unit investment trust: A UIT has a fixed portfolio and isn't designed for intraday trading, margin and short sales.
Sofia wants low-cost, broad index exposu.A hedge fund of funds: An FOF is costly, layered with fees, and not a low-cost index tool.

Which client is the best candidate for a.Age 26, $40,000 net worth, wants long-te: A hedge fund is beyond the means of a small investor seeking growth; a mutual fund fits better.
Which client is the best candidate for a.Retired widow, $300,000 net worth, needs: She needs income and liquidity; hedge funds are for wealthy, sophisticated investors.
Which client is the best candidate for a.Couple saving for college in five years,: Their modest assets and short horizon don't suit an illiquid, high-risk hedge fund.

Which is a recognized drawback of a hedg.It is open only to large institutions: FOFs can actually give nonaccredited investors access to hedge funds.
Which is a recognized drawback of a hedg.Lower correlation with stocks than singl: FOF returns have been more highly correlated with equity markets, not less.
Which is a recognized drawback of a hedg.All its assets sit in one hedge fund str: An FOF spreads money across roughly 10–30 hedge funds for diversification.

The trustee of the Pellham Co. 401(k) pl.A nonparticipating GIC: A fixed-rate nonparticipating GIC is better when rates are expected to fall.
The trustee of the Pellham Co. 401(k) pl.A nonparticipating GIC with a longer ter: Locking a fixed rate for longer is the wrong move if rates are expected to rise.
The trustee of the Pellham Co. 401(k) pl.A nonparticipating GIC with a shorter te: It still pays a fixed rate; only a participating GIC's rate moves with market rates.

Jun invests $3,000 a month in a stock fu.$16.00: That is just the latest price, not the cost of all shares bought.
Jun invests $3,000 a month in a stock fu.$18.75: That is the simple average of the four prices (average price), not average cost.
Jun invests $3,000 a month in a stock fu.$19.50: That is the midpoint of the high ($24) and low ($15) prices.

Ava uses value averaging with a target o.$1,600: $1,600 is what her 80 shares are worth now, not the amount she needs to add.
Ava uses value averaging with a target o.$2,000: Investing a fixed $2,000 is dollar cost averaging, not value averaging.
Ava uses value averaging with a target o.$4,000: $4,000 is the month-2 target value, not the new money needed.

Under Owen's value averaging plan, his a.Buy $750 of shares: The account is above target, so value averaging requires selling, not buying.
Under Owen's value averaging plan, his a.Invest the usual $2,000: A fixed monthly amount is dollar cost averaging; value averaging varies the amount.
Under Owen's value averaging plan, his a.Take no action until next month: Value averaging adjusts every period to hit the target value.

Imani buys 100 shares of a fund each qua.$12,000 invested; $38.30 per share: $38.30 is what DCA-style weighting would give; with equal shares, cost equals the simple average price.
Imani buys 100 shares of a fund each qua.$15,000 invested; $50.00 per share: This prices all 300 shares at the highest price.
Imani buys 100 shares of a fund each qua.$9,000 invested; $30.00 per share: This prices all 300 shares at the lowest price.

Which investor is best suited to share a.A value investor who wants more shares w: Buying more shares on dips is what DCA does; it suits value-style investors.
Which investor is best suited to share a.A saver who needs the same dollar amount: A fixed dollar amount is DCA; share averaging spends more when prices rise.
Which investor is best suited to share a.A hands-on investor who will buy heavily: Buying to reach a target account value describes value averaging.

Which statement about dollar cost averag.It guarantees a profit if continued long: DCA does not guarantee a profit, especially if the price keeps falling and never recovers.
Which statement about dollar cost averag.It beats a lump sum in a steadily rising: In a steadily rising market, investing the lump sum up front buys more shares.
Which statement about dollar cost averag.It requires selling when the account is: Selling to hit a target is a feature of value averaging, not DCA.

Dmitri bought shares of a fund in three.$400.00: That is the specific identification result using the $18 lot.
Dmitri bought shares of a fund in three.$2,000.00: That is the FIFO result using the $10 lot.
Dmitri bought shares of a fund in three.$4,000.00: This treats the shares as having no basis at all.

Rhea bought 500 fund shares for $9,750 p.$1,840: This includes the reinvested dividends but leaves out the $250 commission.
Rhea bought 500 fund shares for $9,750 p.$2,190: This includes the commission but leaves out the $600 of reinvested dividends.
Rhea bought 500 fund shares for $9,750 p.$2,440: This leaves out both the commission and the reinvested dividends.

A fund's management fee is 0.55%, its 12.0.80%: This leaves out the 0.15% of other expenses.
A fund's management fee is 0.55%, its 12.1.05%: Trading commissions are not part of the expense ratio.
A fund's management fee is 0.55%, its 12.4.95%: Sales loads are paid by the investor and are not in the expense ratio.

Lucia puts $10,000 in each of two funds..X: $11,000; Y: $11,500: This adds the percentages instead of compounding them.

A fund's NAV falls 40% in a bear market..40.00%: The gain is earned on a smaller base, so it must exceed the 40% loss.
A fund's NAV falls 40% in a bear market..50.00%: A 50% gain on 60% of the value only gets back to 90%.
A fund's NAV falls 40% in a bear market..60.00%: A 60% gain on 60% of the value only gets back to 96%.

Ava puts 30% of her portfolio in a fund.7.5%: That is the cash portion (30% × 25%), not the stock portion.
Ava puts 30% of her portfolio in a fund.25.0%: This uses the fund's cash percentage instead of applying its stock percentage to her 30%.
Ava puts 30% of her portfolio in a fund.30.0%: This assumes the fund is fully invested in stocks, ignoring manager flexibility.

In early December, Luis plans to invest.Buy now, since only long-time holders ar: Distributions are taxed regardless of how long the buyer has owned the shares.
In early December, Luis plans to invest.Buy now, since reinvested distributions: Reinvested distributions are taxable under constructive receipt.
In early December, Luis plans to invest.Buy Class C shares, which skip capital g: Share class doesn't change the fund's capital gain distributions.

A fund family merges its worst-performin.Survivorship bias that understates past: Dropping losers makes the remaining average look better, not worse.
A fund family merges its worst-performin.Style drift that understates the categor: Style drift is a fund changing its approach, not the removal of failed funds.
A fund family merges its worst-performin.Forward pricing that inflates the surviv: Forward pricing is how mutual fund orders are priced; it isn't a data bias.

Which statement about portfolio turnover.High turnover always leads to large capi: Realized losses can offset gains, so high turnover does not always produce big distributions.
Which statement about portfolio turnover.Funds pass their net realized capital lo: Funds don't distribute losses; they use them to offset gains.
Which statement about portfolio turnover.Trading costs from turnover are included: Commissions, spreads and market-impact costs are outside the expense ratio.

Which pairing of client objective and fu.Maximum safety of principal &rarr; high-: Safety of principal points to government bond funds; high-yield funds carry more default risk.
Which pairing of client objective and fu.Aggressive growth &rarr; U.S. government: Aggressive growth points to small-cap, technology or new-company stock funds.
Which pairing of client objective and fu.High-bracket income seeker &rarr; corpor: High-tax-bracket income seekers are directed to municipal bond funds.
